notes: Independent reading of scan 005 only. Whole source is 2371 x 1689; left half is 1245 x 1689; right half is 1246 x 1689 and begins at whole-image x=1125. Whole, a, b each viewed once, then 23 one-time decision crops. No OCR, web, compilation, other pages, other reader outputs or mathematical recognition tools were used.

The supplied H_drawing.tex was read initially. Its own header assigns it to archive page 5 / PDF page 6, not this scan 005 (H page 4). The parent confirmed the packet association error. It is therefore excluded from the page collation and inventory; its x-loop is not counted as a page discrepancy.

Observed content: an upper chain of free-group-like expressions with t_n-s_n, a rough difference with a low bracket and zero, four F symbols and small maps, a right-column condition labelled C_i, and lower conditions labelled a/b, b prime, c, c prime with homotopy-group injectivity/surjectivity notes. This is a reading description, not a proof of any claim.

No author proof was supplied on this sheet. No theorem, equivalence, or zero calculation was independently verified. The potential missing parentheses, unusual indices and mixed f/g forms were retained from ink rather than corrected by a globular/categorical interpretation. checks is therefore empty.

Authorial corrections include cancelled si on retient/retire, old s beneath exists, cancelled de twice, cancelled que, crossed pi_0 surj, crossed opening forall s,t in F_0, cancelled witness fragment, cancelled f/f_1 before u-v, and cancelled et. The explicit author aside is: "(NB on n'exige pas que g(u)=u\prime)". The source contains no explicit linguistic statement of doubt.

Archive sheet digit 4 is present at bottom left; no author folio, date or title is visible. Entire recoverable main content is handwritten. Pale type-like background traces cannot be securely transcribed as full words; the sheet is classified text, with no reconstructed typed block or invented unreadable-word count.

Own limitations: tiny deleted/overwritten contours remain unresolved where stated. Crop 14 is very tight at the top of the cancelled initial mass; the top was also present in the earlier full-resolution half, but no new certainty is claimed from the clipped crop. Crop 18 clips the very upper part of the f(u) label, which was already read in the half. No crop was repeated.

The literal graphics preserve marks whose mathematical meaning is unassigned. The physical raised dot after crossed D_n and the two points near C_i are not assertions of an exponent or accent. The source drawing rather than a regularized shared-vertex diagram determines the final sketch.

Clear full narrow white channels support doubled F at second/last top terms, lower-right array entry, C_i first F_i prime, E0 existential F_0 and F_1 prime, b existential F_1, and E2 F_1. Clear g forms in the second right-column equality and NB have a low upper bowl and long lower loop. The adjacent first equality f has a taller upper loop. Their mathematical asymmetry is not repaired.

The long b map and several witness maps have convergent right heads. The short u:s-t strokes, b prime source-target link, c u-v, and E2 f(u)-f(v) end bluntly. Top chain arrows point left.
On has a capital oval; NB has no intervening stops; i.e has a visible dot between i and e; inj./inj and surj are preserved as written. The tiny insertion is rp|resp, not silently expanded.
Three stacked contours suggest equiv, with equals retained because retracing may create one apparent extra bar.

Final small sketch has detached endpoints, w and prime separated by the downward stroke, a short lower-right return, and three points below. Two detached curved traces occur below the upper chain. Their significance is unassigned.

brief_feedback: The one-view/one-crop discipline was workable, but the packet included an H drawing whose own page metadata placed it on a different page; this was caught and excluded after the parent confirmed the association error. Several contextual C doubts bundle uncertain alphabet, index and placement; separating those loci in the report is necessary. Very tight crops can clip ascenders (crop 14); retaining the uncertainty is preferable to a forbidden repeat.
